title: Standard Form and Intercepts
short: Graph Ax + By = C quickly using its two intercepts.
trouble: Students find an intercept by setting the same variable to 0 that they are solving for.

blocks.html: Lines can also be written as $Ax + By = C$, called standard form. You get it from slope-intercept form by moving the $x$ term and clearing fractions. It is handy when the numbers are whole, and especially for graphing quickly by intercepts.

The $x$-intercept is where the line meets the $x$-axis, and every point on that axis has $y = 0$. Put $y = 0$ into $Ax + By = C$ and the $y$ term disappears, leaving $Ax = C$. Likewise every point on the $y$-axis has $x = 0$, leaving $By = C$. Two points determine a line, so the two intercepts are enough to draw it.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: $3x + 2y = 12$ crosses the axes at $(4, 0)$ and $(0, 6)$. Plot those two points and the line is done.

blocks.html: For $Ax + By = C$: set $y = 0$ to find the $x$-intercept, and set $x = 0$ to find the $y$-intercept. To convert from $y = mx + b$, clear fractions and move the $x$ term to the left, with $A \ge 0$.

blocks.title: Convert to standard form
steps: Multiply by $-1$ so that $A$ is positive: $2x - 3y = 15$.

blocks.html: Setting the wrong variable to $0$: to find the $x$-intercept you set $y = 0$, not $x = 0$. Check: an $x$-intercept is written $(a, 0)$, so its $y$-coordinate is the one that is $0$.
